changes: The official-source snapshot was refreshed on 2026-06-18 UTC across the tracked set.
NanoClaw shipped a new v2.1 line on 2026-06-17, with v2.1.0 and follow-up patch v2.1.17 published minutes apart.
ZeroClaw materially expanded its install surface in the README, adding preset, app-selection, gateway, prefix, dry-run, and uninstall flows.
PicoClaw posted another nightly build on 2026-06-18 06:16:24 UTC, confirming the lightweight edge lane is still shipping daily.
The monitored set and taxonomy remain unchanged. Hermes stays canonical at https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.
whyItMatters: This was a meaningful run because the strongest movement came from derivative projects, not the category anchor, which is exactly the kind of pressure the watch should catch.
NanoClaw's v2.1 jump signals continued momentum for the security-first, container-isolated branch of the market.
ZeroClaw's broader install and packaging surface matters because better onboarding usually precedes wider adoption, especially for lean Rust alternatives.
PicoClaw's nightly cadence keeps the low-resource edge story active, even without a new stable release.
The right move is to refresh the daily layer and hosted dataset while leaving the stable long-horizon thesis unchanged.
